headline: High-risk write and network overlap: Plandex can modify shared code and git state while Prefect can orchestrate networked workflows, creating dangerous default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can read/write the project directory and uses a review-then-apply flow, while Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume workflow metadata. A shared filesystem or handoff path could let attacker-controlled content influence Plandex’s planning or Prefect’s downstream automation. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Plandex-generated files as workflow inputs without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable project directory, content can cross from one agent to the other.
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Keep Prefect inputs in a separate directory from Plandex workspaces.
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes any Plandex output.
Use read-only mounts for handoff artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all exchanged files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while Prefect also has broad network egress and can call external APIs. If they share a workspace, source code or workflow metadata could be exposed through either agent’s outbound requests. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Plandex reads sensitive source files and forwards them to a model provider, those contents may leave the workspace.
IF Prefect receives the same workspace artifacts and sends them to external APIs, workflow metadata can leak.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Restrict outbound domains for both agents.
Separate code and workflow metadata into different directories.
Review prompts and task inputs before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state exists via the Plandex server backend. Prefect is an orchestration tool that can also coordinate mutable workflow state. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can collide and corrupt state; the default overlap is dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, write conflicts can occur.
IF Prefect mutates files that Plandex is staging, the staged plan can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Pause Prefect runs while Plandex applies changes.
Commit Plandex changes before Prefect starts.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex produces staged changes and can auto-apply them, while Prefect is an automation/orchestration system that may act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats Plandex output as authoritative, an error in the plan can cascade into automated downstream actions. The pair has a clear handoff risk, though not enough evidence for irreversible default harm.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Plandex output without validation, incorrect changes can propagate.
IF Plandex auto-applies a bad plan and Prefect triggers follow-on jobs, the error cascades.
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect acts on Plandex output.
Validate Plandex outputs against a schema.
Log and diff all handoff artifacts.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
requires-engineering: add checksum-based verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Plandex handles model-provider API keys and source code, while Prefect touches workflow metadata, but no specific regulated data class or cross-jurisdiction transfer is evidenced. The compliance pathway is therefore limited and not clearly material.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose retention or residency constraints, verify both agents against them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention settings for each system.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Review vendor DPAs if sensitive data is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing controls.
